items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: I play totally incorrect, Mozart fingering no.

ctx.x: Not the arranging, I was slow. I was a slow arranger. Dick went to Manhattan School of Music. I’m very close with Dick. And he’s a great arranger by the way. I spoke to him some years ago and I said, we were just talking and I said, “I was slow. I went to Berklee a couple of months and I left.” You know so I wrote one chart, “There Will Never Be Another You.” Just straight through, like a little drop two harmony, drop, whatever it

was. Most — I’m a self-taught arranger. And I’m self-taught on the piano. I feel like a little kid. You know Dino Govoni who teaches, he’s a very good saxophone player across the hall from me at Berklee. I played piano once in his room, I was trying out the piano in his room. We all have pianos. And I played for about twenty minutes. He was smiling. He says, “Fred, when you play you’re like a little kid.” He said, and he loves me on saxophone, alto or tenor.
